newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda halting minicar output to save costs - sources.
newsitem.headline: Mazda halting minicar output to save costs - sources.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp is seen pulling out of production and development of mini passenger cars to save on development costs, industry sources say.
Carmakers do not disclose actual development costs for new models, but it amounts to several billion yen.
Minivehicle sales by Mazda, owned 33.4 percent by Ford Motor Co, fell 11.9 percent to 49,178 vehicles in 1996, or 2.9 percent of Japan's market of 1.71 million minivehicles.

On Friday, the economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Mazda would stop production and development of 660cc minivehicles and would procure them from Suzuki Motor Corp for sale under its brand name from autumn next year.
Mazda officials would not comment on the possible pullout.
"We cannot comment about our future new models. We will continue selling minivehicles," a Mazda spokesman said.
Mazda has been selling the Suzuki-made 660cc Scram (Suzuki's Every) commercial vehicles since June 1989 and the 660cc Carol, using a Suzuki-made platform (engine and chassis), since November 1989.
It started selling the Suzuki-made 660cc AZ Wagon (Suzuki's Wagon R recreation vehicle) in September 1994.
Sales of the Carol, which has a Mazda-developed body, fell by about 10,000 in 1996 from the previous year to 17,635 cars, a Mazda spokesman said.
Last October, the Transport Ministry said it would change classifications of minivehicles from October 1998 to make them safer in collisions.

Under the new rules, to be classified as a mini, a vehicle can be no longer than 3.4 metres or wider than 1.48 metres. The current limit for vehicles with a 660cc engine, set in 1990, is a maximum length of 3.3 metres and a width up to 1.4 metres.
